title: Label-Free Peptide Nucleic Acid-Based Electrocatalytic Biosensor Coupled with EXPAR for Ultrasensitive Detection of miR-181b
content: Osteosarcoma (OS) is the most common primary malignant bone tumor in adolescents, and its early diagnosis remains difficult because micrometastases are not readily detected by imaging or biopsy. Exosomal microRNAs are stable in body fluids and are attractive markers for liquid biopsy; miR-181b is abnormally expressed in OS, but its low abundance in body fluids and its high sequence homology with miR-181a/c/d place stringent demands on analytical sensitivity and specificity. Here, we report a label-free electrocatalytic electrochemical biosensor that couples a peptide nucleic acid (PNA) capture probe with the exponential amplification reaction (EXPAR). A 3′-thiolated PNA probe was immobilized on a gold electrode through rapid freezing-assisted Au–S bonding, and EXPAR converted the target into abundant single-stranded DNA that hybridized with PNA and a signal probe to form a sandwich structure. Because PNA is electrically neutral and DNA is negatively charged, [Ru(NH₃)₆]³⁺ was electrostatically adsorbed onto the sandwich, and its signal was amplified by [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻ mediated electrocatalytic recycling and recorded by square wave voltammetry. Under optimized conditions, the sensor responded linearly to miR-181b from 1 fM to 1 nM with an experimental detection limit of 1 fM and a theoretical 3σ detection limit of 1.2 aM. It effectively discriminated miR-181b from miR-181a/c/d, and showed an electrode-to-electrode RSD of 3.39%.
